Wind gust was measured by the KF05 AWOS station at the Vernon Airport. This wind gust may have been due to a dry microburst.
The local high school sustained some roof damage. Some highway signs and trees were also downed.
One tree was blown over with other trees having limbs blown down. A couple windows in a store were blown out and an awning was blown over a house. Monetary damages were estimated.
Several large trees and power lines downed. Monetary damages were estimated.
Major transmission lines were blown down. A barn was destroyed and two houses had their roofs blown off. Monetary damages were estimated.
A train engine and a following car filled with grain were blown over. The incident occurred at the intersection of FM 1763 and HWY 287. Monetary damages were estimated.
The hail reportedly damaged several cars. Monetary damages were estimated.

Several storm spotters reported a tornado near the Wilbarger and Wichita county lines. The tornado blew a vehicle into the path of a pickup on Highway 287. The driver of the car received minor injuries and was taken to an Electra hospital for treatment. The tornado also destroyed…
Penny size hail covered the ground near the intersection of county roads 2073 and 2074.
Highway 287 had to be closed due to transmission lines lying over the roadway. Monetary damages were estimated.
The hail broke a windshield of a vehicle on Highway 287 near the Hardeman and Wilbarger county line. Monetary damages were estimated.
The wind gust caused minor roof damage, as well as minor tree and power line damage. Monetary damages were estimated.
The hail was reported at the intersection of Highway 287 and Farm Road 925.
Golfball-size hail was reported on Highway 287 on the north side of Vernon. The hail was covering the roadway.
Golfball- to tennis ball-size hail was reported.
The hail was reported near FM 1924 and County Road 85N.
Several power poles were downed. Monetary damages were estimated.
The hail was reported in White City.

Damage was reported to several barns and storage buildings, with numerous trees and power poles/lines also downed. An empty mobile home was severely damaged as well. The damage was reported from the Green Acres subdivision west of Vernon, southwest to Lockett. Monetary damage est…
Minor structural damage occurred to a building. Power line damage was also reported. Monetary damages were not available.

A storm chaser east of Davidson OK observed and photographed a partially rain-wrapped tornado to his south-southwest, estimated to be just south of the Red River in far northeastern Wilbarger County Texas. This tornado produced no known damage.
Several tree limbs were downed, with the largest being around 5 inches in diameter. Monetary damages were estimated.
This tornado began over far northern Wilbarger county before quickly moving into Jackson county, OK and continuing into Tillman county. No known damage occurred with this portion of the tornado.
Power lines were downed near the corner of CR 134 E and Highway 183.
Emergency manager reported 2 inch hail. Reports of 1.25 inch and 1.75 inch hail were also received within Vernon city limits between 7:06 and 7:11pm CST.
Multiple reports of a tornado near Harrold. Tornado last approximately two minutes and did very minor damage to power lines and power poles.
Very brief tornado reported by storm chaser. No damage reported.
Hail size ranged from quarter to half dollar size with smaller hail covering the ground.
At least one tree blown down.
A storm chaser and a law enforcement officer reported a brief tornado estimated to be 10 miles west-northwest of Vernon. No damage was reported.

Law enforcement and a storm chaser reported a tornado that moved from approximately 4 miles northwest of Lockett to near Lockett. Trees were damaged and the roof was damage from a metal building (DI 21; DOD 3).
A storm chaser observed a destroyed metal barn and power poles snapped about 6 miles northwest of Grayback. All of the damage and debris was observed to be from west to east.
Nickel to quarters with some half dollars mixed in.

The tornado that began in northeast Hardeman County moved through the far northwest corner of Wilbarger County before crossing the Red River into Jackson County Oklahoma. No damage was known to have occurred in this rural area Wilbarger County.

The tornado crossed from Jackson County Oklahoma into far northern Wilbarger County between Odell TX and Elmer OK, before crossing the Red River for the third time back into Jackson County Oklahoma. Again, no damage is known to have occurred in this portion of Wilbarger County.
Irrigation pivot blown over by wind.
No damage reported. Report relayed via emergency manager.
A tornado was observed and videotaped by a storm chaser, and was estimated to have occurred approximately 3 to 4 miles south-southwest of Oklaunion. No damage was reported.
A spotter reported a tornado about 8 miles south of Vernon. No damage was reported.
No damage reported. 60 to 70 mph winds estimated.
A storm chaser observed a tornado north of Vernon. No damage is known to have occurred and the time and location are estimated.
Billboard blown over along US-287, and large trees were damaged at Eastview Cemetery. Time estimated by Radar.

A swath of strong thunderstorm wind damage occurred northeast of Oklaunion. Tree and house damage was noted on county road 117 N just north of US-287, near US-287 and county road 128 E, and along FM-1763.
Powerlines and powerpoles downed. Time estimated from radar.
Large limb downed, video on social media.
Semi truck blown over near the Hardeman/Wilbarger county line.

This tornado initially developed in southeast Hardeman County and moved into Wilbarger County west of Lockett. This may have been a series of tornadoes across southeast Hardeman and far western Wilbarger Counties as the condensation funnel was not visible at times. However one ch…

This tornado was observed developing about 2 miles east-southeast of Lockett. Soon after developing, it caused significant roof damage to a home 2.5 miles east-southeast of Lockett on FM-433. Outbuildings were destroyed southeast of here along FM-433 and County Road 95 S. Tree, p…
Three storm chasers reported a tornado that was observed from a long distance. The tornado lasted about a minute, and produced no known damage, so the location is estimated.
Small limbs snapped off of trees.
Two inch tree limbs broken off of tree.

The long-lived Lockett tornado moved into Wilbarger County from Foard County and continued to move northeast. As the tornado approached County Road 138, the tornado created significant tree damage and roof damage to a home, and destroyed an outbuilding. Along County Road 138, at …
Image showing a large section of a metal roof facade removed from a motel building. Time is radar estimated.

Numerous storm chasers observed a brief tornado in southern Wilbarger County estimated to be about 2 miles west of US-183/283 and a mile or two north of the Baylor County line. No damage is known to have occurred.
